title: Workforce scaling & price-shock scenarios (Jul 2026)
content:
Executive summary:
This workbook outlines 3 operational scenarios for H2 2026–Q2 2027 combining workforce scaling plans with pricing shock responses. Purpose: give leadership an actionable playbook that ties headcount phasing to unit economics and pricing levers so Finance + GTM can rapidly execute triggers if demand or cost dynamics change.

Key assumptions (base case unless noted):
- ARR mid-2026 baseline: $120M recognized run-rate
- Gross margin target (current): 58%
- Avg fully-burdened cost per engineer: $250k/year; non-eng (sales/CS/product): $180k/year
- Average time-to-hire (eng): 10 weeks; recruiter funnel attrition 30%
- LTV/CAC elasticity approx 6–8 (derived from growth cohort analysis, see linked models)
- Price sensitivity baseline: demand elasticity -0.8 for hosted API customers, -0.3 for enterprise Dedicated contracts

Scenario definitions:
1) Baseline (plan): continue approved hiring cadence, minor pricing tweaks for non-core tiers.
- Hiring: +45 net hires FY Q3–Q4 2026 (30 eng, 15 non-eng) per approved budget.
- Pricing: 5% list increase for premium usage tiers Jan 2027 (delayed), no immediate increases.

2) Price Shock (demand shock + price squeeze): macro slows, we face 12% sequential drop in usage units over 2 quarters and 6% upwards cost pressure on GPU cloud pricing.
- Response: price action + targeted hiring pause + capacity cushion drawdown.
- Hiring: freeze non-critical hires and delay 60% of open reqs (net +18 hires instead of +45).
- Pricing: immediate selective price uplift (hosted API consumption tiers +8%) with targeted credits for strategic accounts to retain ARR.

3) Aggressive Growth (capacity-first): demand outstrips baseline, need to accelerate hiring to capture GTM moments and increase dedicated capacity.
- Hiring: accelerate to +80 net hires in H2 2026 (55 eng, 25 non-eng); temporary use of contract engineers and outsourced onboarding to reduce time-to-ship.
- Pricing: temporary promotional credits for new customers to drive pipeline; later conversion to standard pricing.

Headcount plan (quarterly snapshots):
- Legend: ENG = engineering, SRE = site reliability, DS = applied ML/Research, GTM = sales + CS + marketing, OPS = finance/legal/people ops
- Q3 2026 (net hires in quarter): ENG: +18, SRE: +4, DS: +6, GTM: +10, OPS: +7 (total +45)
- Q4 2026 baseline: ENG: +12, SRE: +3, DS: +4, GTM: +3, OPS: +3 (total +25)
- Q4 2026 price-shock: ENG: +6, SRE: +1, DS: +2, GTM: +6, OPS: 0 (total +15)
- Q4 2026 aggressive: ENG: +30, SRE: +6, DS: +8, GTM: +10, OPS: +6 (total +60)

Projected incremental annualized opex by scenario (rounded):
- Baseline: +$9.5M payroll run-rate by EOY (net of ramp and hires)
- Price Shock: +$3.8M payroll run-rate by EOY (hiring freeze reduces incremental spend)
- Aggressive Growth: +$16.8M payroll run-rate by EOY (including contractor premium)

Pricing sensitivity matrix (hosted API volume):
- Elasticity (ε) = -0.8 (baseline) used for hosted; enterprise reserved contracts elasticity -0.3
- Table (hosted API traffic):
  Price change | Expected volume change | Net revenue delta vs baseline
  -10%         | +8%                   | -3%
   -5%         | +4%                   | -1%
    0%         | 0%                    | 0%
   +5%         | -4%                   | +1%
   +8%         | -6.4%                 | +0.8%
   +12%        | -9.6%                 | -0.5% (inflection point for hosted)
Note: because of mixed customer base, blended inflection point for net revenue improvement is ~+6–9% depending on shift to enterprise mix.

Unit economics sensitivity (illustrative):
- Baseline token cost per 1M tokens processed: $3.20 (infrastructure + model licensing + ops)
- If GPU spot costs +6% -> token cost becomes $3.39 -> gross margin falls by ~1.4 pts on current mix.
- Hiring acceleration (add 50 engs) increases payroll burden by ~+$12.5M/yr; to maintain margin need either +12% effective price or +18% throughput efficiency via batching/quantization improvements.

Trigger framework (operational runbook):
- Trigger A: Usage falls >7% MoM and ARR churn >1% (30d) -> Action: implement hiring pause Tier 1 (freeze all non-critical reqs), reduce non-essential cloud burst capacity, and prepare targeted price uplift templates. Owner: VP Finance + Head of People Ops.
- Trigger B: Spot GPU cost up >8% vs baseline for 14 days -> Action: increase routing to cheaper model variants (quantized variants), enable cache-heavy policies, delay low-priority batch jobs. Owner: Head of Serving Runtime + Infra.
- Trigger C: Pipeline conversion rate rises >20% QoQ -> Action: accelerate hiring to SRE/Eng; authorize contractor budget and reduce hiring approval latency (fast-track). Owner: Head of GTM + VP Eng.

Recommended immediate actions (next 30 days):
1) Build a monthly pricing-test calendar with A/B buckets for hosted tiers (finance + growth). Owner: Olivia Chen. Due: 2026-08-01.
2) Create a hiring-priority matrix: label every open req as critical / deferrable / pause. Owner: Priya Nair (People Ops). Due: 2026-07-26.
3) Run a 2-week cost-sensitivity simulation in the cost-model repo with +6% GPU and -10% hosted volume assumptions. Owner: Ben Kline (FP&A). Due: 2026-07-30.
4) Prep communications + pricing legal templates for a selective hosted uplift of up to 8% with grandfathering options for enterprise contracts. Owner: Legal + Rev Ops. Due: 2026-08-10.

Appendix: quick math snippets and checkpoints
- Break-even price increase to offset +$12.5M payroll: Current revenue base $120M => +10.4% price on blended revenue needed (assuming no elasticity). With elasticity -0.8 blended effect, realistic net revenue gain at +10% price would be ~+2.4% -> doesn’t cover payroll delta alone. Hence need combined paths: efficiency + selective pricing.
- Time-to-hire adjustment: if we shorten eng TTH by 20% (use contracting + sourcing), near-term ramp cost rises by ~+$1.2M but long-term revenue capture could exceed that assuming conversion from accelerated features.

Notes / open questions:
- Need updated cohort LTV/CAC and churn sensitivity to price changes (request to Growth Analytics: ANALYTICS-328).
- Are there contractual constraints that prevent >5% price changes for certain enterprise cohorts? Legal to confirm list by 2026-07-25.

References / links: see linked_artifacts above. Also related internal analyses: "unit-economics-hiring-flow-sensitivity-q3-2026" and "demand-elasticity-trigger-rules-and-hc-flex-protocol" (Drive).

Next steps for this doc: convert into a compact slide deck for Exec review (10 slides), and a 1-page TL;DR for the CEO. Assign owners and due dates in the linked JIRA ticket JIRA-FIN-2026.

Prepared by: Samir Rao (Finance) — working draft for exec and people ops review.
